body: Can't reproduce, neither with compatibility nor with Metal renderer. M4 Pro, macOS 26.0.1 (25A362).
Hm, strange. I tried clearing my SCons cache with `scons --clean` and then rebuilding off master and the issue persisted... Later today I'll see if I can bisect the issue.

I was able to reproduce it in VM with macOS 15.7, so probably specific to this macOS version.

Reproducible with 4.6.dev2, ~but not with 4.6.dev1 and 4.5.1. Will try bisecting later.~ Inconclusive, 4.6.dev2 and custom build from master crashed exactly once, so it's impossible to tell if 4.6.dev1 is really OK. None of the bisected builds crashed, so there's no point to continue.

I tried to start it via the debugger (vs code)

```
        "type": "cppdbg",
        "request": "launch",
```

Tried 10 times, not reproducible.


The debugger delays it too much, "Threading Issues" I think:
`libsystem_pthread.dylib             0x0000000197d8eb74 start_wqthread + 8`

It's not Godot thread, but something created by OS, so it's likely something with OpenGL driver (which is deprecated since 10.14).

If you can consistently reproduce it, please check if it's reproducible when using ANGLE for compatibility mode. For custom build, [download static libs](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-angle-static/releases/) and build with `angle_libs=path_to_extracted_static_libs` flag. Run Project Manager with `﻿﻿--rendering-driver opengl3_angle` (and set in the project setting for the project).

OK, I'll check right away. I was also able to crash it using the `lldb` debugger (without vscode extensions).

`DisplayServer::can_create_rendering_device()` in the main thread, this might be the reason, it seems like it's crashing when checking if Vulkan is supported or not (by creating and destroying rendering device). So it might be an issue with having both GL and Vulkan contexts in the same app. We might need to run this check in a separate process like we do on Windows (since it was also crashing in some conditions).

So it's likely the same issue as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/103518 and https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/101659 but for macOS (if it's and issue on Windows and Linux, I guess it's not surprising it's the same on Mac).

> and build with `angle_libs=path_to_extracted_static_libs` flag. Run Project Manager with `﻿﻿--rendering-driver opengl3_angle` (and set in the project setting for the project).
